_precacheMaxBytesComment: PR #353 integrated with #356-358 (2026-09-06): preserve both bounded allowances over the 4840192-byte baseline: +2048 bytes for shared inactivity and +67840 bytes for the offline clinical library. Total 4910080; no additional merge allowance. PR #374 adds an explicit 2 KB safety allowance for sync-notification orchestration changes and transient TSX diffing in the authenticated bootstrap path. Auth monitoring and calculators stay cached; documents remain outside precache under docs/ and templates/. No new exclusions or relaxed warning bands. Auth evidence/rollback: docs/AUTH_ACCESS_MODEL.md; library evidence: src/features/clinical-library/README.md. Clinical library v2 (2026-09-06): +31744 bytes (0.65%) more for the transfer cover, the critical medications sheet and three additional scores inside the lazy ClinicalLibraryDrawer chunk (84.8 KB), kept in the precache so they work offline. PR #384 adds a bounded 8192-byte allowance for explicit Eloisa page-state/freshness messaging and clinical-coverage validation; it adds no ignored asset pattern. Total 4952064. PR #1010 adds only 40960 bytes for the measured Zod 4 security upgrade (vendor 55634 to 94434 bytes, total precache +38875 bytes); new total 4993024. All offline assets remain cached. See docs/BUNDLE_RISK_LEDGER.md. Owner-approved raise (2026-10-25, option C): +38912 bytes, new total 5031936. It precaches vendor-firebase-functions (12028 bytes) and the new shared-runtime-loaders chunk (2008 bytes); splitting those loaders out of the online-only Rayen chunk removed the need to precache that 43 KB chunk. It also makes room for #1026 (about 16.3 KB, specialist notes bound to patient and episode) and #1022 (about 5.8 KB, unreadable identity), leaving about 9 KB of margin. See docs/BUNDLE_RISK_LEDGER.md. PR #1034 integration (2026-10-26): allocate another 8192 bytes of the owner-approved approximately 78 KiB option-C envelope, for 47104 bytes used since the 4993024-byte baseline. Measured candidate precache 5037813 bytes in 246 entries, 5877 over the previous cap; new margin 2315 bytes. This preserves note/day replay, refusal, retry and ACK guards offline. No assets excluded, no other budgets raised. A third Terser pass saved only 357 bytes and was reverted. See docs/BUNDLE_RISK_LEDGER.md.

assetPatternBudgets._comment: Browser ExcelJS is served as a runtime asset instead of a duplicated Vite chunk. This ceiling keeps the measured ~948 KB asset near the warning band so payload drift stays visible without blocking the current release.

startupChunkBudgets.label: firebase-core
startupChunkBudgets._comment: Raised from 320000 to 350000. The chunk sat at 91% of the older ceiling with Firebase SDK 12; minor Firebase patch releases were landing on the edge of the budget. Upstream-controlled size, so give explicit headroom. Revisit if utilization exceeds 93%.

startupChunkBudgets.label: app-authenticated-shell
startupChunkBudgets._comment: PR #469 allowed 625000 bytes for confirmed-cache protection. PR #481 allowed 627000 bytes for episode-aware metadata. The compact specialty control beside the census summary measures 628453 bytes against 626182 bytes on main (same local lockfile); allow 630000 bytes with rollback and guardrails documented in docs/BUNDLE_RISK_LEDGER.md. Other budgets remain unchanged. PR #892: same local toolchain measures base b0262b91e at 630000 bytes and the queue wakeup candidate at 630254 bytes (+0.041%). Allow only 400 additional bytes; see docs/BUNDLE_RISK_LEDGER.md. Phase 1a P4a: base 257900995 measures 628935 bytes and the split-day write hygiene 631549 bytes (+0.42%); the conflict auto-merge needs it synchronously in this chunk, so raise only this ceiling to 632000 bytes; see docs/BUNDLE_RISK_LEDGER.md.

chunkPatternBudgets._comment: PR #1010: Zod 4.6.7 fixes GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5. Measured vendor size 94434 bytes; keep validation available offline with a dedicated 96000-byte ceiling. The bounded 40960-byte precache allowance and rollback are documented in docs/BUNDLE_RISK_LEDGER.md.
Kept in sync with the firebase-core startup budget above.

Callable Functions are precached since 2026-10-25 (owner-approved budget raise): browsers that keep a failed dynamic import until reload (WebKit, Firefox, Chromium <=153) stalled every callable write after a flaky first load. Callables still need the network; the shared loader rejects offline before calling. Keep the dedicated runtime bounded so dependency drift remains visible.
PDF.js worker/runtime remains async, but this protects the large PDF viewer chunk from silently drifting toward the global chunk limit.
PDF.js text/import runtime is async and must stay out of the PWA precache. This dedicated budget keeps PDF.js drift visible separately from app-level PDF chunks.
PDF.js worker is a large async runtime asset excluded from install-time precache. Keep it governed separately so worker drift is visible without misclassifying it under the generic JS chunk ceiling.
PDF vendor chunks are async but among the largest payloads; keep a dedicated ceiling so PDF library drift stays visible before it reaches the global chunk budget.

HEIC/HEIF conversion is loaded only for high-efficiency mobile prescription photos and kept out of the PWA precache. A dedicated ceiling preserves release visibility without relaxing the global chunk budget.
Online-only, read-only Eloisa document repository opened explicitly from the clinical drawer.
Online-only Eloisa clinical drawer loaded only after an explicit patient action.
Online-only Eloisa sync history panel, loaded when the operator opens it.

Offline-capable census library drawer (catalog, transfer cover, critical medications sheet, calculators, nine scores) loaded only after pressing Documentos. Measured 84831 bytes on 2026-09-06; the ceiling leaves room for more documents and scores while keeping drift visible.
Optional diagnostic console formatter, dynamically imported only while auditing. Core measurements and all clinical functionality remain in precache.
Online-only Rayen import workflow, deferred out of the census startup. Measured 202 KB; the ceiling keeps drift visible without relaxing the global chunk budget.
Optional monthly Excel download, loaded on demand like the existing ExcelJS runtime. Keep growth bounded without increasing install-time payload.

Optional Eloisa source-table parser, episode annotations and validation. Measured 17861 bytes; bounded separately without raising the existing 12000-byte core export ceiling. Loaded only for an attached source, outside install-time precache.
